beats.direction: Use the recurring witness with an on-screen disclaimer: CITY CONTEXT / NOT DAY-SPECIFIC.
beats.voice: Copenhagen turns participation into an evidence problem: admission, time, teardown, rights, screening, product data and institutional memory each demand a record. This chapter follows commerce: Between runway attention and an order sit identifiers, line sheets, showrooms, buyer permissions and product records whose adoption is often claimed faster than it is proved.
beats.onScreen: Then: The EU adopted ESPR in 2024, establishing a framework that includes Digital Product Passports; the Commission identifies textile apparel as a priority product group.
beats.credit: Scandinavian Academy of Fashion Design · CC BY-SA 4.0

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: The EU adopted ESPR in 2024, establishing a framework that includes Digital Product Passports; the Commission identifies textile apparel as a priority product group. That earlier record fixes a point in time; it does not prove an inevitable progression toward the present.
beats.onScreen: Now: The Commission says the DPP Registry launched in July 2026 with user-interface and API registration, access management, logging and machine-readable vocabulary support.
beats.credit: Graphic © Rayven-Nikkita Collins; sources in claim ledger

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: The distinction is material. A polished interface can survive after its workers, contracts, specifications or permission trail disappear, leaving the audience with an outcome but not its operating history.
beats.onScreen: Next: The presence of EU infrastructure does not prove that every CPHFW garment already carries a textile DPP or that one event-level product-data stack has been selected.
beats.credit: Graphic © Rayven-Nikkita Collins; sources in claim ledger
